sensors.title: RGB camera
sensors.measures: A colour picture of what is in front of the lens, one red/green/blue value per pixel.
sensors.typical_use: Object detection, following a line, recording training images, teleoperation views.
sensors.prim_type: Camera (UsdGeom.Camera); RtxCamera/CameraSensor add OmniSensorAPI when reading
sensors.data: get_data('rgb') -> (H, W, 3) uint8 array (warp; .numpy() for numpy).
sensors.needs: Nothing physical; it just has to be under the link it should move with and not inside a mesh.

sensors.title: Depth camera
sensors.measures: How far away things are: one distance per pixel, measured from the camera's image plane.
sensors.typical_use: Obstacle avoidance, grasping, measuring distances, building 3D maps.
sensors.data: get_data('distance_to_image_plane') -> (H, W, 1) float32 in stage units; inf where nothing is hit.
sensors.api_6_1: isaacsim.sensors.experimental.rtx: RtxCamera, CameraSensor (or SingleViewDepthCameraSensor for stereo-style depth)
sensors.needs: Same as the RGB camera; set the near clipping distance below the closest thing it must see.

sensors.title: RTX lidar
sensors.measures: Laser distance points all around (or in front of) the sensor: a 3D point cloud each scan.
sensors.typical_use: Mapping (SLAM), localisation, obstacle detection for mobile robots.
sensors.prim_type: OmniLidar (omni.usd.schema.omni_sensors), loaded from a lidar USD asset
sensors.needs: A config/asset name (e.g. 'Example_Rotary'); the asset loads from the Isaac assets root.

sensors.title: IMU (inertial measurement unit)
sensors.measures: Acceleration (m/s^2 on a metre stage), turning speed (rad/s) and orientation of the body it sits on.
sensors.typical_use: Balance and tilt for legged robots and drones, odometry, detecting bumps and falls.
sensors.needs: An enabled rigid-body ancestor (a robot link with Rigid Body); press Play to get readings.

sensors.title: Contact sensor
sensors.measures: Whether the body is touching something and how hard (force in newtons on a metre/kg stage).
sensors.typical_use: Foot contact for walking robots, bumpers, detecting a successful grasp.
sensors.needs: An enabled rigid-body ancestor with colliders; on PhysX that body gets PhysxContactReportAPI.

result.how_sensors_attach: A sensor is a child prim of a robot link, so it moves with that link. The 'offset' is its position in the link's own frame; rotation turns it relative to the link. USD cameras look along their local -Z axis with +Y up; Isaac robots usually drive forward along +X with +Z up.

glossary.meaning: OmniGraph is Omniverse's visual programming system; each graph is saved in USD as an OmniGraph prim with node prims inside.
A node is one box in the graph; its node:type says what it does (for example omni.graph.nodes.SetVariantSelection).
An event node (On Keyboard Input, On Tick, On MessageBus Event, ...) starts a chain of execution.
An execution wire says what runs next: when one node finishes, the node its exec output is wired to runs.
A data wire hands a value (a token, number, path ...) from one node's output to another node's input.
An Action Graph (evaluator 'execution') does nothing until an event node fires; then execution flows from node to node.

result.explanation: The timeline runs from time code 0 to 0 (0 time codes = 0 s at 24 time codes per second; played at 24 frames per second). 0 attribute(s) on 0 prim(s) have time samples. A time code is a frame number on the stage timeline; seconds = time code / timeCodesPerSecond. framesPerSecond is only how fast players step through it. Keep them equal so one time code is one frame. Value resolution: the strongest layer with an opinion wins, and inside it time samples beat the default value at every frame (the default is only used at the Default time or when there are no samples). Between samples USD interpolates linearly (quaternions take the shortest arc); before the first and after the last sample it holds the nearest one.
